threads_text: Apple is hiring someone to build an AI agent that uses your Mac the way a capable person would: apps, websites, commands, even code. site_article.headline: Apple job listing points to an AI agent that can operate a Mac
site_article.dek: A senior engineering manager posting describes an agent that browses the web, works across apps, runs commands and writes code, according to Bloomberg and TechCrunch.
site_article.summary: Apple has posted a job listing for a senior engineering manager to oversee an AI agent that can use a computer, Bloomberg reported on November 19, 2026. Bloomberg also said Apple has considered launching the service as soon as the end of 2027.
site_article.seo_title: Apple AI agent for Mac: what the job listing reveals
site_article.seo_description: An Apple job listing describes an AI agent that uses a Mac like a person: apps, web, commands and code. What Bloomberg reported and the possible 2027 timing.
site_article.answer_summary: Apple appears to be building its own AI agent that can operate a computer on a user's behalf, based on a job listing Bloomberg found. Bloomberg reported that Apple has eyed a launch as soon as the end of 2027, and development is described as early.

paragraphs.text: Apple is looking for a senior engineering manager to lead work on an AI agent that can use a computer, according to a job listing that Bloomberg reported on November 19, 2026. TechCrunch, which followed the Bloomberg report the same day, said the agent would carry out computer work on a user's behalf, including using apps, visiting websites and writing code.

The listing asks candidates to imagine an agent that operates a computer the way a capable person would. As quoted by TechCrunch, the posting says the agent browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code and calls services, choosing the right tool for each step. It also says the work should be done privately and with the polish people expect from Apple.

According to TechCrunch, the posting describes agents that move between tools and carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code and APIs. Superpower Daily, summarizing the same listing, said the assistant would plan tasks with several steps and pick tools as it goes, and noted that the listing gives no technical detail on how user information would be protected.
Neither report gives a name or codename for the project. TechCrunch said progress on the in-house agent remains in the early stages and that Apple did not respond to its request for comment.
Timing and limits on outside agents

Bloomberg reported that Apple has eyed introducing the service as soon as the end of next year, which TechCrunch relayed and Superpower Daily described as the end of 2027. Superpower Daily called that timing tentative and noted that Apple has not announced a release date.

At the same time, Apple is making it harder for third party agents to take full control of a Mac, according to Bloomberg's reporting as summarized by TechCrunch. The upcoming macOS 27.3 will show warnings that discourage users from granting full access to outside agents. TechCrunch added that Apple told developers in October that it planned additional controls over granting apps that level of access.

Agents that do computer work for people have become a crowded field. TechCrunch noted that Anthropic and OpenAI have launched such services and that Meta has introduced its Muse line of agents, and it framed Apple's effort as part of a broader push to expand its AI products under chief executive John Ternus.

The two moves fit together. If Apple limits how much control third party agents can get on macOS while it builds its own, its agent could end up with deeper access to the Mac than rival tools, presented as a privacy and safety measure. The job listing's stress on privacy points the same way, although Apple has not said how it would handle user data.

The next concrete sign will be macOS 27.3: how strongly its warnings discourage full access for outside agents will show how much room Apple plans to leave for tools from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta on the Mac.
